issues.legal_issue: Land acquisition proceedings do not lapse under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act when possession has been taken, even if compensation has not been paid.

A long delay in filing an appeal may be condoned on a liberal, justice-oriented approach when the case’s circumstances, including the land’s use for an important public purpose, provide sufficient grounds.
A policy governing fresh acquisition proceedings applies only where the acquisition has been validly held to have lapsed.
When an acquisition under the 1894 Act remains valid, the landowner is not entitled to compensation under the 2013 Act but remains entitled to compensation determined under the 1894 Act award.
